objective:
Task SS4.2: Rewrite the "Delegate" subsection of `.claude/commands/continue-development.md` (under its "Delegate -> Verify -> Track -> Continue-or-stop loop" heading) to use the sdlc-supervisor framework's task-packet + implementer-agent mechanism for sdlc-tracked work, instead of always spawning a `general-purpose` subagent with free-text scope. Condensed design context you need (do not read design-spec.md/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md yourself -- this is already distilled for you):

1. TWO TRACKING CONVENTIONS (already established by SS4.1's rewrite of the Resume section, immediately above Delegate in the same file -- do not change that section, just be consistent with the vocabulary it already uses): 'sdlc-tracked' work is any task whose id appears in `.sdlc/state.json`'s `work_items[].tasks[]`. 'legacy proposal-folder' work is everything else (tracked only via `docs/proposals/<slug>/{DESIGN_SPEC,IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN,PROGRESS}.md`, no `.sdlc/state.json` entry). This SS4.2 rewrite applies the new packet+implementer mechanism ONLY to sdlc-tracked work. Legacy proposal-folder work keeps using today's existing Delegate behavior unchanged (spawn `subagent_type: general-purpose`, paste the task's scope/acceptance-criteria text inline) -- generalizing the implementer agent to arbitrary proposal folders is explicitly out of scope for this task; `.claude/agents/implementer.md` currently hardcodes `docs/sdlc/*` doc names as things it must never read, so it is not yet a generic delegate target for other proposals.

2. WORKING-TREE-CLEAN PRECONDITION: the implementer agent (`.claude/agents/implementer.md`) runs directly in the shared repository working tree, not an isolated worktree (a deliberate, already-made decision, not something to reconsider here). Because there is no filesystem isolation, the Delegate step must refuse to spawn an implementer for an sdlc-tracked task when the orchestrator's own working tree is not clean (`git status --porcelain` produces any output) -- surface the dirty state to the user instead of spawning into it. This recovers the protection worktree isolation used to provide for free.

3. TASK PACKET GENERATION: for the chosen sdlc-tracked task, generate a task packet via `scripts/sdlc/generate-task-packet.mjs` (read that script's own header comment, in your read_paths, for its exact CLI usage -- it takes `--task-id`, `--plan-entry-file`, optional `--design-excerpt-file`/`--dependencies`/`--out`, and writes JSON matching `docs/sdlc/schemas/task-packet.schema.json` to `.sdlc/task-packets/<task_id>.packet.json`). The generator's `read_paths`/`write_paths` inference is a documented-honest heuristic, not semantic understanding, and has previously produced wrong output that needed hand-correction (a prior real task's generated packet mis-parsed a design excerpt into a bogus read-path entry, dropped a leading `.` from a filename, and inferred a read-only doc as a write target). The rewritten Delegate section must say explicitly: review and correct the generated packet's `read_paths`/`write_paths`/`forbidden_paths`/`acceptance_criteria`/`verification_commands` before use; a packet containing the literal string `"NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW"` anywhere, or any path that's plainly wrong on inspection, must never be handed to an implementer as-is -- fix it by hand first (writing the packet file directly is fine when the heuristic's output would need substantial correction anyway).

4. ACTIVE-PACKET BOOTSTRAP (this is the actual mechanical crux of this task): the committed `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/sdlc-path-check.mjs`, read it -- it's in your read_paths, especially its header comment section 2 'WHICH PACKET IS ACTIVE') denies ALL `Edit`/`Write` calls from an `agent_type === "implementer"` caller unless it can resolve exactly one active task packet. The simplest resolution path for a single implementer running in the shared tree (not a worktree) is a pointer file: a single line containing the task id, written to `.sdlc/active-packet` in the repo root. The rewritten Delegate section must say: before spawning the implementer, write `.sdlc/active-packet` containing exactly the task's id (nothing else) into the shared working tree; after the task's completion report has been accepted (in the Verify/Update-tracking steps that follow Delegate -- already covered by other sections, do not rewrite those), delete `.sdlc/active-packet` so it does not linger and get mistaken for the next task's active packet. If the task is abandoned/blocked, still remove or overwrite the pointer once the orchestrator has decided what happens next, rather than leaving a stale pointer.

5. CONCURRENCY: `.sdlc/project.yaml`'s `budgets.max_concurrent_implementers` is `1`, and only one `.sdlc/active-packet` pointer can exist at a time. The rewritten section must say: sdlc-tracked tasks are delegated strictly one at a time via this mechanism -- never batch multiple sdlc-tracked tasks into concurrent implementer spawns the way the current Delegate text allows for independent tasks in general. (Legacy proposal-folder tasks, still using `general-purpose`, keep whatever batching behavior the section already describes -- do not remove that for the legacy path.)

6. SPAWNING: for an sdlc-tracked task, spawn `subagent_type: implementer` (not `general-purpose`) and paste the FULL packet JSON verbatim into the spawn prompt (the implementer's own instructions say every invocation hands it exactly one task packet 'pasted into your prompt at spawn time' -- it does not read the packet file itself, and per its own rules never reads `docs/sdlc/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `docs/sdlc/design-spec.md`, or `docs/sdlc/PROGRESS.md` directly; the rewritten section should say this explicitly so a future orchestrator run doesn't accidentally tell an implementer to 'go read the plan').

7. RETRY / RESUME SEMANTICS (a real gap hit twice already in this project's own history, must be stated explicitly, not left implicit): if an implementer's completion report is `blocked`, or a run is interrupted mid-task and needs to continue, the correct way to resume it is `SendMessage` addressed to that exact agent's own id (it already has the full packet and context in its own memory) -- never a brand-new `Agent` call that merely references the prior run's context by unverified claim ('you already did X, now do Y'). A fresh agent has no legitimate basis to trust such an unverifiable continuity claim, and correctly refuses it, which wastes a spawn and produces a confusing refusal rather than a clean resume. If the original agent is genuinely gone (session ended, id lost), the correct recovery is a brand-new `Agent` spawn with the COMPLETE packet pasted inline again as a fresh attempt -- never a message asserting prior partial progress the new agent cannot verify.

8. EXPERTISE-SKILL STEP (design-spec's revised, non-unilateral version -- replaces whatever the current Delegate text says, if anything, about creating skills; if the current text has no such step, add this one): the orchestrator may write a one-run inline instruction into an implementer's spawn prompt freely, no review needed, and it dies with that run if not reused. If the orchestrator notices the SAME one-run instruction recurring across multiple tasks, it may DRAFT (write to disk, but not enable/reference/activate) a project-local expertise-skill file capturing that recurring instruction. Drafting is not activating: turning a drafted skill into something actually used, or committing it into the project, requires a human check-in first (same tier as a design-spec sign-off) -- the orchestrator never activates a skill unilaterally just because it drafted one.

9. SCOPE-CHANGE HANDLING: the rewritten section should note that a completion report with `status: scope_change_requested` is something the orchestrator (who has the full plan context, unlike the implementer) must judge on its merits -- a real gap in the task's scope vs. the implementer overreaching -- never auto-approved into more work and never silently ignored.

Write the actual prose into the existing 'Delegate' subsection of `.claude/commands/continue-development.md`, matching the file's existing voice/formatting conventions (bullet lists, bold lead-ins, etc. -- look at the surrounding Verify/Update-tracking/Continue-or-stop sections for the house style). Do not renumber or restructure sections outside 'Delegate'.
non_goals: Do not modify `.claude/agents/implementer.md`, `.claude/agents/verifier.md`, `.claude/hooks/sdlc-path-check.mjs`, or any schema file -- those are already correct and out of scope for this task.

Do not extend the task-packet/implementer mechanism to legacy proposal-folder work (work with no `.sdlc/state.json` entry) -- that path keeps today's existing `general-purpose` delegation behavior unchanged.

Do not modify the 'Orient', 'Resume in-progress work', 'Pick new work', 'Scaffold new work', 'Verify', 'Update tracking', or 'Continue or stop' sections of `continue-development.md` -- those are separate tasks (SS4.3/SS4.4) or already done (SS4.1) or out of this task's scope entirely.

Do not implement SS4.3 (verifier routing) or SS4.4 (run-budget stopping conditions) -- the Delegate rewrite should not attempt to also cover verification routing or budget-based stopping; those remain separate, later tasks.

Do not actually run/test the rewritten Delegate section against a real task packet+implementer spawn -- this task only edits the command file's prose; the orchestrator will exercise the new behavior on a subsequent real run as its own verification, not as part of this packet's `verification_commands`.
acceptance_criteria: The 'Delegate' subsection is rewritten so that, for sdlc-tracked work, the orchestrator: (a) refuses to spawn an implementer if `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, surfacing the dirty state instead of proceeding; (b) generates a task packet via `scripts/sdlc/generate-task-packet.mjs` (or writes one by hand when the generator's heuristic output needs correction) into `.sdlc/task-packets/<task_id>.packet.json`, and explicitly reviews/corrects any inferred `read_paths`/`write_paths`/`forbidden_paths`/`acceptance_criteria`/`verification_commands` before use -- a packet containing the literal `NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW` placeholder or an inferred-but-wrong path must never be handed to an implementer as-is; (c) writes a single-line `.sdlc/active-packet` pointer file containing the task's id into the shared working tree before spawning, and removes it once the task's completion report has been accepted or the task is abandoned -- never left lingering into the next task; (d) spawns `subagent_type: implementer` with the full packet JSON pasted verbatim into the prompt, not a pointer telling it to go read the packet file itself; (e) delegates sdlc-tracked tasks strictly one at a time (never batches multiple sdlc-tracked tasks into concurrent implementer spawns), consistent with `max_concurrent_implementers: 1` and the single `.sdlc/active-packet` pointer.

For legacy proposal-folder work (no matching `.sdlc/state.json` entry), the rewritten section preserves the existing behavior (spawn `subagent_type: general-purpose`, paste task scope/acceptance-criteria inline, allow batching independent tasks) essentially unchanged -- the packet/implementer mechanism is explicitly scoped to sdlc-tracked work only in this rewrite.

The rewritten section explicitly documents the resume/retry procedure: use `SendMessage` to a specific blocked/interrupted implementer's own agent id to resume it (never a fresh `Agent` call that references prior context by unverified claim); if the original agent is genuinely unavailable, the correct recovery is a brand-new `Agent` spawn with the complete packet pasted inline again, never a message asserting unverifiable prior progress.

The rewritten section includes the non-unilateral expertise-skill step: freely writable one-run inline instructions (no review, dies with the run); drafting (never activating) a project-local expertise-skill file when the same one-run instruction recurs across tasks; activation/commit of a drafted skill requires a human check-in.

The rewritten section states that an implementer is only ever given the pasted packet, never told to read `docs/sdlc/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `docs/sdlc/design-spec.md`, or `docs/sdlc/PROGRESS.md` itself.

The rewritten section notes that a completion report with `status: scope_change_requested` requires the orchestrator's own judgment (real plan gap vs. scope creep), never auto-approval into more implementer work.

No section of `continue-development.md` other than 'Delegate' is modified (Orient, Resume in-progress work, Pick new work, Scaffold new work, Verify, Update tracking, and Continue or stop all remain byte-for-byte unchanged).
No file other than `.claude/commands/continue-development.md` is modified.
